text: Oh! A visitor! Mind the specimen jars. And the snake. He's friendly. Mostly.
Ibbie Crane, naturalist, at your service. Have you seen a blue-striped frog? No? Pity.
The jungle's alive, captain. Every leaf. I've catalogued three hundred and twelve species. Three hundred and thirteen if that beetle on your boot is new.
My favourite collector! The parrotfish are thriving in their bucket. I named one after you.
Shh! The fireflies are courting. Come back at dawn. Or stay very, very still.
Rain's wonderful for frogs. Terrible for paper.
Parrots, monkeys, snakes, jaguars, and a beetle that glows when it's upset. I upset it often, for science.
The monkeys can be befriended with melon, by the way. They're terrible thieves but wonderful company.
Only if you're slow, careless or tasty. Jaguars hunt further at night. Snakes bite, and the bite makes you sick. Carry milk!
Less dangerous than Saltmarrow on a Friday.
The stepped temple's older than anything else on the island. The Temple Guardian still walks its lower halls, I'm told.
The carvings show people with fish-scale skin bringing gifts to the sea. The First Tide, the scholars call them.
